claim_falsified: An exact global optimum over regular (nonsingular-nuisance) finite labelings is one-point exchange-stable under ANY feasibility convention, so DS18.2's finite stability step needs no convention. FALSE off the null set: on this support-minimal N=4 table from the named off-(L) law, both exact global regular optima reach the single nuisance-singular labeling by one admissible relocation whose DS11 pseudo-inverse value exceeds the regular optimum by exactly 1/96. The in-bin (DS9) convention -- singular destinations are infeasible -- is therefore load-bearing and must be named. This does not refute DS18, whose law makes such tables null.
construction: Take X=(-1, 0, 1/2, 1/2) and Z=(-1, 1, -3/4, 1/4) in S=(X, 3X^2-1+Z); every row lies on the named law's support and the score table is exactly centered. The labeling (0,0,1,2) is one of exactly two exact global optima over regular labelings, both with value 1/12. Moving row 0 from cell 0 to cell 1 (source stays nonempty) reaches the labeling (0,1,0,2), whose binned nuisance block is exactly zero; its DS11 pseudo-inverse value is 3/32.

exact_quantities.support_minimality: K=3 requires N>=4 for any nonempty-preserving move; N=3 has three singleton cells and zero admissible relocations.
exact_quantities.minimality_search: All 91,390 four-row tables over the 40-point grid {-1,-1/2,0,1/2,1} x {-1,-3/4,-1/2,0,1/4,1/2,3/4,1} were enumerated exactly: 84 host a singular labeling and 42 have the escape from every global regular optimum, 14 of them exactly centered.

boundary_scope: This is a convention boundary, not a counterexample to DS18.

At d_lambda=1 a zero binned nuisance block forces every cell lambda-sum to vanish, hence sum_i S_lambda_i = 0, which has probability zero under the named continuous law; almost surely every three-nonempty-cell labeling is regular and this table cannot occur.
Under the project's in-bin (DS9) feasibility convention the displayed move is inadmissible, so the global regular optimum is ordinary one-point exchange-stable as DS18.2 states.

Distinct from CE-DS-DEGENERATE-GLOBAL-TIE-001, which compares values at N=8 on a Gaussian-derived table; this fixture exhibits the gap as an admissible one-point relocation from every global optimum, on the DS18 law's own support, at the minimal support size.
